In this nomenclature the superscript symbol indicates whether the protein is present at < 5% of normal expression (^o), diminished in expression (^−), i.e. between 5% and 20% of normal expression, or normally present but nonfunctional (^+)

Based on the CD18 expression on neutrophils, LAD1 was sub-classified into three phenotypes viz. severe (LAD1°) with CD18 expression <2% moderate (LAD1^-) phenotype with CD18 expression 2%–30%, and mild (LAD1^+) phenotype with CD18 expression ≥30%.

phenotype_specificity.statement: P51 (PMID 33391282) is in the severe LAD1° class with umbilical cord separation recorded as "Yes", features the paper names as typical. Only ITGB2 was sequenced for LAD1 patients. A0025 has no clinical data.

These patients usually present in infancy with delayed separation of the umbilical cord, omphalitis, and necrotic infections of the skin and mucosal surfaces (5).
Molecular confirmation was performed was done using Sanger sequencing for LAD1 and next-generation sequencing (NGS) for LAD3.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Batch HGVS: nonsense, p.(Tyr530Ter), agreeing with both papers (p.Tyr530X; p.Tyr530Ter). The paper describes the disease as caused by decreased expression or function of CD18.

quotes.quote: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].
Usually, this leads to the absence or decreased expression of the β_2 integrins on the leukocyte surface, but sometimes a normal expression of nonfunctional β_2 integrins is found.

Direct Sanger sequencing of the ITGβ2 gene revealed 57 disease-causing variants in 105 patients (Table S2), including 30 patients we have previously reported (18).

concerns: PMID 22134107 is a mutation-update table (Table I) without case descriptions: people are identified only by database accession numbers, and sex, age and clinical features are not given per person.

In Table I the LAD-I type and the families (alleles) count belong to the table row (the variant), not to one accession number; for an accession number listed with a second variant, the expression class reflects the person's genotype, not this allele alone.

A0025 is cited in Table I to reference [3] (Roos and Law 2001), so it was published before 2001; P51 is from a 1990-2020 Indian retrospective cohort. Whether they are the same person cannot be told from these papers; the 2001 source was not available here.
Homozygosity is presumed (A0025) or implied by the absence of a heterozygous mark (P51); neither paper reports parental testing.
notes_for_panel: Two carriers in two papers; possible but unconfirmed overlap.
